_comment: ADOPT (rc.14 · WS6): the service-level expectations for continuous assurance, mounted as docs/governance/assurance-sla.json and owned by the second line. A signal from any declared source opens a CASE (assurance-case-check.mjs); the case must be assessed within the severity's window, remediated by its deadline, and — for a runtime breach (high/critical) — record a CONTAINMENT action (suspend routine autonomy, block release, rollback, model fallback, quarantine income, or suspend the product offering). An open breach past its deadline blocks unless the second line risk-accepts it. Tune the windows to your risk appetite; the Loom validates and reconciles — the accountable decision stays human.
_vocabulary_is_data: `sources` and `containment_actions` are VOCABULARY: the gate checks a case's source and containment against these lists and knows nothing else about them, so an institution extends both by editing this file and never by editing a gate. Delete the entries you do not run — an adapter nobody feeds is a source of nothing, and leaving it listed lets a case claim it. `shariah-compliance-monitoring` is the continuous-monitoring feed a Shari'ah compliance function files against its own book (the standard requires the monitoring to be continuous, not periodic); the harness reads the records that feed produces and never watches production, so a quiet period is UNCOVERED here, not clean. Two of the containments park VALUE rather than code: `quarantine-income` holds suspect income in a charity-pending account until a purification record disposes of it (income parked is not income booked, and it is never booked as income later); `suspend-product-offering` halts new sales of a product whose structure no longer conforms while the existing book runs off. Both are generic containments — a mis-priced fee, a mis-sold rider or a structurally non-conformant contract reach for the same two — and a repo that declares neither is unaffected.
